records.Title: Tiles
records.Desc: There are a total of 108 tiles in the game, divided into three suits: Dots, Bamboo, and Characters, with 36 tiles in each suit. Players can form a Pong (triplet) and a Kong (quad), but cannot make a Chow (sequence). Players take turns playing their tiles in counterclockwise order.

records.Title: Winning a Hand
records.Desc: A winning hand may contain no more than two suits. There is no limit on the number of wins; feel free to win as many times as you can before the game ends!

records.Title: Three Tile Pass
records.Desc: After dealing the tiles, each player selects 3 tiles of the same suit to randomly exchange with another player (either clockwise, counterclockwise, or with the player opposite).

records.Title: Deficient Suit
records.Desc: After dealing the tiles, players must choose one suit as the Deficient Suit. The Deficient Suit can only be discarded and cannot be used to make a Pong, Kong, or to win. Once designated, the Deficient Suit cannot be changed during the game, so choose carefully.

records.Title: Kong
records.Desc:
Playing 4 identical tiles is called a Kong, which comes in three types: 
1. Exposed Kong: When you use a discarded tile to form three identical tiles in your hand, you can declare a Kong.
2. Kong from Exposed Pong: When you already have an Exposed Pong and later draw the fourth tile from the wall, you may declare a Kong.
3. Concealed Kong: When you hold four identical tiles (having drawn the fourth tile), you may declare a Kong.

records.Title: End of the Game
records.Desc: The game ends when all tiles have been drawn. Players with a Deficient Suit (also known as “Three Suits”) and players not holding a Ready Hand must accept additional penalties.

records.Title: Geng
records.Desc: Having four identical tiles in your hand counts as one Geng. When you win, the score is doubled for each Geng you hold.

records.Title: [Self-Drawn]
records.Desc: Winning by drawing a tile yourself.

records.Title: [Kong-Drawn Win]
records.Desc: Winning by drawing a tile immediately after declaring a Kong.

records.Title: [Kong-Triggered Win]
records.Desc: After declaring a Kong, discarding a tile that allows another player to win.

records.Title: [Stealing a Kong]
records.Desc: Winning by claiming the tile that another player has drawn to complete their Kong. The Kong being stolen will not be counted in the score.

records.Title: [Win by Last Catch]
records.Desc: Winning by drawing the last tile from the wall.

records.Title: [All Pongs]
records.Desc: A winning hand consisting of four triplets (or Kongs) and a pair.

records.Title: [All One Suit]
records.Desc: A winning hand composed entirely of tiles from one suit.

records.Title: [Seven Pairs]
records.Desc: A winning hand composed of seven pairs.

records.Title: [Heavenly Hand]
records.Desc: 32 Faan. When the dealer wins immediately after dealing out the tiles.

records.Title: [Earthly Hand]
records.Desc: 32 Faan. When a non-dealer wins in the first round after drawing their tiles. Before drawing tiles, actions like Pongs or Kongs cannot occur, and Heavenly Hands and Earthly Hands are not counted for any other scoring.

records.Title: Chow / Sequence
records.Desc: Three tiles of the same suit that are in consecutive numerical order.

records.Title: Pong / Triplet
records.Desc: Three identical tiles.

records.Title: Kong
records.Desc: Four identical tiles.

records.Title: Pair
records.Desc: Two identical tiles.

records.Title: Winning a Hand
records.Desc: To win, you must hold 13 tiles plus one tile either drawn by yourself or discarded by another player, thus forming one Pair and four Chows or Triplets.

records.Title: Pong
records.Desc: You can declare a Pong if a tile discarded by another player can form a Triplet with the tiles in your hand. If you miss the opportunity to Pong, you cannot Pong the same tile again before your next draw.

records.Title: Kong
records.Desc: You can declare a Kong if a tile discarded by another player can be used to form a Kong with your tiles. A successful Kong allows you to win double the base score from the discarding player.

records.Title: Kong from Exposed Pong
records.Desc: When you already have an Exposed Pong and later draw the fourth tile from the wall, you may declare a Kong. When you do this, you can win points from the other three players.

records.Title: Concealed Kong
records.Desc: When you hold four identical tiles (having drawn the fourth tile), you may declare a Kong. When you do this, you can win double the base score from the other three players.

records.Title: Chuck
records.Desc: Discarding a tile that allows another player to win.

records.Title: Score Transfer
records.Desc: When a player declares a Kong and subsequently discards a tile that allows another player to win, the points from the Kong must be transferred to the winning player. In cases of multiple wins from one discard, the player who declared the Kong pays multiple times.

records.Title: Refund
records.Desc: At the end of the game, players who are not in a winning position (Unready Hand) will return all points earned from Kongs. If there has been a Score Transfer, the Refund is not required.

records.Title: Check Unready Hands
records.Desc: At the end of the game, players who are not in a winning position (excluding Three Suits) must pay the maximum possible multiples to players who are ready to win but did not achieve a win, in addition to the Self-Drawn multiples.

records.Title: Check Three Suits
records.Desc: At the end of the game, a player who has a Deficient Suit in their hand is called Three Suits. Three Suits players must pay 16 times to each of the other players.
